lesson.subtitle: Lesson 12 -- Monday and Wednesday
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Ricardo Coutinho | Lesson 12 -- Monday and Wednesday
lesson.grammar_point: prepositions of time: on (days, dates) / in (months, parts of the day)

listenings.text: Hi Ricardo, this is Amy, from the Miami office. A quick message about next week. Monday is a holiday in the United States, so the office is closed. The team meeting is on Tuesday, not on Monday, at ten in the morning. On Wednesday, the director is in New York, so there is no meeting. Your call with São Paulo is on Thursday, in the afternoon. Have a nice weekend!

Hi, this is Paul, from the fourth floor. A small piece of advice about dates in the United States. Here, we write the month first, and then the day. So five, ten is May tenth. It is not the fifth of October. In Brazil, it is the other way. At a bank, this is very important. Check the date two times, every time. It is a small thing, and it saves a big problem.

extra_audio.text: It is Sunday night, and I open my calendar. On Monday, I have a meeting at nine. On Wednesday, I have English class. On Friday, I go to the beach with my family. Now my week is on the calendar.

lesson.pre_a1_modelo: On Monday, I have a meeting.
